name: fdsq
comment: MAREK'S FREEDRAW-BY-EDGE-TYPE PROPOSAL, on the square grid. Today a drawn edge is marked by inserting a degenerate two-sided tile: freedraw's alphabet is literally {A2 digon, A4 square}, the digon marking a drawn edge. That is a workaround for an alphabet that can say 'tiles meet at a vertex' but cannot say anything about an EDGE, and it costs degenerate faces, extra degree-2 vertices and a bigger alphabet. With edge types the property goes on the edge instead: split the one edge type into a DRAWN and an UNDRAWN variant, glue like to like, and ink only the drawn ones. Six tiles, all the unit square, differing only in which of their edges are drawn — the six binary necklaces of length 4 up to the dihedral group (0000, 1000, 1100, 1010, 1110, 1111). Both variants have length 1: the geometry is the plain square grid, and the marking is carried entirely by the edge type. Angles in D=24 units: 90 = 6.
